div.head: Hn 62.1
div.ab: Ab Aduentu Domini usque ad octabas Epiphanie et a Septuagesima usque ad XV dies post Pascha et festis diebus et Quatuor temporum et diebus Quadragesimalibus et aliis legittimis ieiuniis et in diebus Ueneris et uigiliis sanctorum Apostolorum non est tempus leges faciendi, id est uel iusiurandum pro fidelitate domini uel concordia[m] uel bellum uel ferri uel aque uel alias legis examinaciones tractari;
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 583 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: vgl. Summa leg. Norm. 80: Sunt tempora in quibus leges non debent fieri nec simplices nec aperte, uidelicet omnia tempora in quibus matrimonium non potest celebrari. Ecclesia autem legibus apparentibus omnes dies treuge ecclesiastice prohibet ac defendit, uidelicet ab hora nona in die Iouis usque ad ortum solis in die Lune subsequente et dies IX lectionum ieiuniorum, Quatuor temporum. Hn steht zwischen diesem weitgehenden Gottesfrieden und Cnut, während E Cf. 2 die Treuga erst Sonnabend Mittag beginnt

cf. Summa leg. Norm. 80: Sunt tempora in quibus leges non debent fieri nec simplices nec aperte, uidelicet omnia tempora in quibus matrimonium non potest celebrari. Ecclesia autem legibus apparentibus omnes dies treuge ecclesiastice prohibet ac defendit, uidelicet ab hora nona in die Iouis usque ad ortum solis in die Lune subsequente et dies IX lectionum ieiuniorum, Quatuor temporum. Hn stands between this far-reaching Truce of God and Cnut, whereas in E Cf. 2 the Treuga begins only at noon on Saturday

div.ab: From Advent until the octave of Epiphany, and from Septuagesima until fifteen days after Easter, and on feast days and on the Ember days and on the days of Lent and on the other lawful fasts, and on Fridays and on the vigils of the holy Apostles, it is not the time for making laws, that is, for dealing either with an oath for fealty to a lord or with agreement [?] or with the duel or with the ordeal of iron or of water or with other tests of law;
